# Contribute to the Outlanders 2 guide

This is a community-maintained reference with reviewed changes. Pages are generated from data files; they are not edited directly in the browser.

## Report a correction

Open a [content correction](https://github.com/kellan/outlanders2-wiki/issues/new?template=content-correction.yml) form. It asks for the page, what it currently says, your proposed correction, how you know, the game version, and evidence. To report something you measured or saw in play without proposing a specific text change, use the [gameplay observation](https://github.com/kellan/outlanders2-wiki/issues/new?template=gameplay-observation.yml) form; every research page links to it with the entry filled in. A screenshot of the field guide or a reproducible gameplay test is useful. Describe starting conditions and what you actually observed. You do not need to change code to contribute.

The [GitHub repository](https://github.com/kellan/outlanders2-wiki) is public. Everyone is welcome to report corrections and contribute through issues and pull requests.

## Make an edit

1. Create a branch for one correction or closely related set of changes.
2. Find the entry with `npm run content:find -- pumpkin`, or browse the content folders. Every article page also ends with a "Suggest an edit" link that opens its JSON record in the GitHub editor, and a "Report a problem" link that starts a correction issue for that page.
3. Edit the JSON record, preserving its stable ID and source references. Add evidence for factual changes.
4. If you changed a building recipe or gameplay block, run `npm run content:derive` to refresh the stored `made_from` recipes on resources. Run `npm ci` once (it installs the search indexer), then `npm run build` and `npm test` (optional for small browser edits; the pull request checks run both).
5. Run `npm run dev` and review the changed page and its links at the local address printed by the server.
6. Open a pull request describing what changed, why, the evidence, and the checks you ran.

Node.js 18 or later is required. There are no third-party runtime packages to install.

## Where to edit

- `content/buildings/`: one building or plant per file; names, descriptions, worker limits, and linked processes.
- `content/resources/`: one resource per file; names, satisfaction fields, and provenance.
- `content/scenarios/`: one scenario per file; descriptions, objectives, day limits, build/plant lists, and need switches.
- `content/leaders/` and `content/biomes/`: one entry per file.
- `content/observations/`: one sourced claim or open question per file.
- `content/collections.json`: ordered lists of record files. Add a new record here without changing existing IDs or casually reordering entries.
- `content/reference/`: shared catalogs, recipes, source exports, and extraction metadata. Most corrections should not require editing these files.
- `src/`: page rendering, stylesheet, and document shell.
- `assets/`: game icons and gameplay evidence screenshots, copied into the site by the build.
- `dist/`: the generated site. It is not committed; `npm run build` creates it locally and the deploy workflow publishes it after a merge.

Files use stable IDs rather than titles, so renaming Pumpkin does not break its links to scenarios. Use readable names in the `name` field; preserve internal identifiers for matching records.

## Evidence and uncertainty

Use the in-game field guide for displayed names, recipes, construction requirements, and worker slots. Use scenario data for stored objectives, building lists, and need switches. Use controlled gameplay observations for actual timing, yields, consumption, and behavior. A stored value is not automatically a measured gameplay result.

Record a new claim in `content/observations/`. Each record needs an ID, target type and ID, claim, status, and evidence with a kind, game version, date, and reference. See `content/observations/clay-pit-late-start.json` for an open question. Supported statuses are `open`, `confirmed`, and `disputed`. Supported evidence kinds are `player-report`, `field-guide`, `gameplay-test`, `decoded-data`, and `official-source`.

Observation records appear in the article's research notes. They do not automatically replace gameplay facts. If a claim is confirmed, update the appropriate content field and explain how the evidence supports that change. Do not mark an observation confirmed just because it sounds plausible.

Preserve contradictions. For example, the Bakery field guide and decoded process balance differ on fuel consumption. Record both rather than silently choosing one. If a factual correction changes a decoded objective, update its validation status and retain the original evidence; do not leave a claim that the changed values match the original bytes.

For scenario needs, omitted means unspecified; it does not mean false. For crops, use the exact scenario planting list. A sandbox biome reference alone does not establish normal crop availability. Unknown values must not be replaced with zero.

## Sizes and distances

Write every size and distance a player would measure in **game squares**, the cells of the placement grid as the game draws them: a crop field is 1 × 1, a fruit tree 2 × 2, a Basic House 2 × 2. The stored building grid (`GridDimensionsBehaviour`) uses two units per square, so stored dimensions are halved for display; on the site this goes through `footprint()` in `src/app.js`, and a test fails if a page prints stored dimensions anywhere but the raw research notes. When a stored distance or count has not been shown to use the same grid (tree seeding range, wild-spawn density, sandbox map sizes and construction tiles), show the stored number labelled "grid units" or "stored", never as squares, and add a row to INFORMATION-NEEDED until play confirms the unit.

## Share a level strategy

Level pages have a Strategy section for community advice: a summary, a suggested build order and things to watch out for. Use the [level strategy form](https://github.com/kellan/outlanders2-wiki/issues/new?template=level-strategy.yml) (every level page links to it with the level filled in). A maintainer converts the submission into `content/strategies/<level id>.json`, which has `summary`, `build_order` (building IDs with a note each), `pitfalls`, `status` (`draft` until someone has finished the level that way, then `reviewed`), `game_version`, `date`, `contributor` and `source`. Strategies are rendered apart from decoded data and labelled as community advice. Keep them specific to the level, and do not restate objectives the page already shows.

## Suggest a link

The Guides elsewhere page points at strategy guides, walkthroughs, videos, tools and communities on other sites. Use the [link form](https://github.com/kellan/outlanders2-wiki/issues/new?template=external-link.yml). A maintainer adds accepted links to `content/links.json` (`id`, `title`, `url` (https), `site`, `type` one of `guide`, `walkthrough`, `video`, `community`, `official`, `tool`, `covers`, optional `levels` by id or name, `language`, `date_checked`, `status` `needs-check` until a maintainer has looked, then `listed`, and a one-line `note`). Level pages show the links that name them. Links are community pointers and are never cited as evidence for a decoded fact; a weekly check removes dead ones. We do not list copies of this wiki, paywalled pages or advert farms.

## Spoilers and unreleased content

Use `content/spoilers.json` to place confirmed or explicitly reported unreleased content in the Spoilers section. Each entry records its target, classification, date and reason. Related content can be withheld as `related-release-unconfirmed` without asserting it is unreleased. Use the existing availability record and explain the evidence. Do not infer unreleased status merely from an unfamiliar name or presence in the game files. Keep uncertain release status distinct from spoilers.

How unreleased status is established: each prefab in the game files carries a `MinGameVersion` gate on its `SerializedKeyBehaviour`; the game hides objects whose gate exceeds the running version. `content/reference/decoded-mechanics.json` (`min_game_version.roots`) records the gate of every prefab root and the installed game version. Mark an entry `confirmed-unreleased` only when its own prefab root stores a gate above the installed version (32 against 30 in the baseline build), and cite that in the reason. A maintainer or player report alone gives `reported-unreleased`. Scenarios, biomes or seasons that only exist for gated content but carry no gate of their own stay `related-release-unconfirmed`. A gate at or below the installed version does not prove public release on every platform; the release history in `availability.json` supplies dates where known.

Do not expose spoiler names in ordinary index pages, search results, or related-entry lists. Test both the Spoilers page and the regular catalog when changing an availability record. Use a neutral issue or pull-request title when the details contain spoilers.

## Images and private information

Use only necessary evidence images, with the game version and source noted. Crop out account details and personal information. Do not upload game executables, complete asset bundles, decompiled assemblies, save games, credentials, or machine-specific logs. Game artwork and text have separate rights from the site's code; see the publication notes before adding redistributable assets.

## Before requesting review

Add a changelog fragment: a new file `changelog/unreleased/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` holding one paragraph that says what a reader will see and the page to look at, ending with the pull request number in brackets. One file per change means two pull requests never edit the same line. `npm run changelog` shows the assembled log; the maintainer runs `npm run changelog:release` after merging a batch, which moves the fragments into `changelog/<date>.md` and rewrites `CHANGELOG.md`. Reasoning and provenance go the same way: a new file `content-notes/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` (older notes stay in `CONTENT-NOTES.md`). New tests also go in their own file, `scripts/checks/<pr-number>-<slug>.mjs`, which asserts on import and is run by `scripts/check-fragments.mjs`; editing an existing assertion in place is fine, but don't append new blocks to the end of the big check scripts.

Keep the change focused. Check names, numbers, links, evidence, and spoiler classification. List unresolved questions honestly. The maintainer reviews and merges changes. A merge to `main` builds, tests and publishes the website automatically; the pull request checks run the same build and tests, so browser-only edits get feedback without a local Node install.

## Licensing and attribution

Submit original code and editorial contributions under the project’s MIT license. Only contribute material you have the right to license. Identify game-derived text, artwork and other third-party material and preserve its attribution: these are excluded from MIT. We retain game artwork and text as reference material without claiming ownership. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md for the boundary.

# Changelog

What changed on the wiki, newest first, with the page to look at. Entries live as one file per change under `changelog/` so pull requests never collide: add `changelog/unreleased/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` with one paragraph; `npm run changelog:release` dates a batch on merge. The game's own version history is on the [Changelog page](https://outlanders2wiki.com/changelog/) under "Game updates" (`content/history.json`). Reasoning and provenance stay in `CONTENT-NOTES.md`.

## Unreleased

- Tournament Mode lists every season’s 14 rewards with the Reward Points each needs, including the live Rural season, decoded from the reward lists packaged with the game (80).
- Levels are easier to browse: the home page links each campaign and each of the six challenge types, every challenge type has its own page explaining what it is and when it runs, and All levels is one sortable table (79).
- Site search: a search box in the top bar on every page, with results filtered by section (buildings, food, levels, mechanics and so on) (78).
- Text is larger and easier to read, tables line up, and wide screens get more room (77).
- Pages now carry their own search description, canonical address, link-preview image and structured data, and the site publishes a sitemap, robots.txt, an llms.txt guide for AI assistants and a proper 404 page (76).
- Campaigns & levels now splits campaign levels from challenge levels, and groups the challenges by type: Original, Redux and Bounty in the current rotation, and the older Chill, Ranked and Remix sets with their release dates (every two weeks from July 2024 to March 2025). The Challenges page explains the rotation (74).
- Icons are back to the earlier style; the game-composited set from #72 is withdrawn. The Buildings page subtitle links work (issue 62).
- More playtest results: one mug of Beer refills a villager's Fun from low to full, which supports the stored Fun 4 over the 2 the field guide shows; 20 Fishing Dock casts at the 0–2 spot gave 1.35 Meat a cast, and a dock stops at 72 Meat; a Trading Outpost trade was no faster with three workers; and the Tropiclands and Winterlands outposts' field guides match the stored trades (issue 10).
- The home page leads with the biome islands and gives every section a game icon, with small icons beside building, plant, resource and food links and portraits beside leaders (#70).
- Seven more buildings are checked against the in-game field guide: the four houses, Playground, Zen Garden and Fitness Park. A finished Bakery's refund (5 of 9 Clay, 2 of 4 Stone) shows demolition gives back half of each material, rounded up. A timed Trading Outpost trade confirms you get one import at a time and puts a trade at about three quarters of a game day (#69, issues 10 and 31).
- Footprints now count in-game squares: a crop field is 1 × 1, a fruit tree 2 × 2, a Basic House 2 × 2. Before, they showed the stored grid units, which are twice as fine. Distances whose unit isn't confirmed, such as tree seeding range, now say "grid units" instead of "tiles". The Food page adds food per square, where crops beat trees, and drops columns that said the same thing on every row. Plant pages also say whether a field is one plant (Potato: 3 Veggie) or several (Carrot: 3 plants, 1 each) (#68).
- New [Sandbox](https://outlanders2wiki.com/sandbox/) page in Mechanics: the three starting-population presets, the three map sizes, the map generator's 15 buildable tiles and 3 food sources per villager, and each biome's crops, fruit trees, forestry plants and extra need (#67, issue 29).
- The demolition test now asks for a Bakery (9 Clay + 4 Stone) to check whether "half back" holds for other buildings and how odd amounts round; the Basic House result is already recorded (#66, issue 31).
- The plants list loses its junk "Base" row, and Cypress Tree and Willow Tree move to Spoilers: the game files gate them to a future update. An audit found every other unlisted building is a real campaign building. zBeer Stand is now shown as Beer Stand (#65).
- The Trading Outpost now shows each biome's trade as a choice: Evergreen gives 12 Wheat for 6 Glass Pane *or* 6 Animal Hide, not both as the page said before. A table compares the Tropiclands, Evergreen and Winterlands trades, a short explainer covers how a trade runs, and the unused base and test-only versions are hidden (#64).
- Building, DairyFarm and Stock no longer have pages. They are internal or test-only prefabs that never appear in play (#63, issue 62).
- Icons now show white glyphs with dark lines, as in the game, instead of letting the tile colour show through; the fill is computed from the game's own outlines until the game's fill layer is exported. The home page has Mechanics and Reference boxes alongside Buildings and Plants (#61).
- The [Needs](https://outlanders2wiki.com/needs/) page is now a short hub: one table of the eight needs, each linking to its own page ([Food](https://outlanders2wiki.com/needs/food/), [Community](https://outlanders2wiki.com/needs/community/) and so on) with its meter, the items and places that restore it, and where it applies. Eating has its own page, [How eating works](https://outlanders2wiki.com/eating/). Old links to sections of the Needs page still land in the right place (#60).
- Findings from the local agent's play session: field guides for 38 more buildings, all checked against the game files (the [Trading Outpost](https://outlanders2wiki.com/buildings/trading-outpost/) trades 12 Wheat for 6 Glass Panes and 6 Animal Hides), what demolishing a [Basic House](https://outlanders2wiki.com/buildings/basic-house/) gives back, the day counter turning at dawn, a five-day meal log on [Needs](https://outlanders2wiki.com/needs/), the Drylands and Winterlands planting menus, the Rural season rewards, and confirmed campaign level order. Pages now show a "Seen in play" section (#59).
- [Guides elsewhere](https://outlanders2wiki.com/guides/) gains what a web search turned up: the Outlanders 2 Fandom wiki, YouTube level walkthroughs, Apple's launch notes and the App Store listing. Links for the first game, including the Steam discussions (Outlanders 2 is not on Steam), sit in their own section. All are marked not yet reviewed (#58, issue 38).
- The whole site now uses the in-game field guide's look: the game's stored colour palette and its interface font, Bricolage Grotesque; a dark mode that follows your system, with a toggle in the top bar; icons on tiles in their game category colour; and a field-guide card on every [building page](https://outlanders2wiki.com/buildings/open-kitchen/) laid out like the game's: each icon in its own colour, any-of inputs under one bracket, and Provides with the need values the guide shows. Table sorting now works on the published pages (#57, issue 56).
- A [Mechanics](https://outlanders2wiki.com/mechanics/) section replaces the Needs link in the menu: new pages for [Happiness](https://outlanders2wiki.com/happiness/) (weights, the Boost, levels with a target), [Villagers and life](https://outlanders2wiki.com/villagers/) (ages, births, days to starve or freeze), [Heat, cooling and water](https://outlanders2wiki.com/heat-cooling-water/) (heat sources, Tropical weather), [Days and time](https://outlanders2wiki.com/time/) (a game day is five minutes, shifts, day limits) and [Gear](https://outlanders2wiki.com/gear/), with Needs, Houses and Gathering places grouped under it (#55, issue 1).
